messages:
sam: @support quick one — ACME says their user sees a 403 when switching between projects in the dashboard. They can list org-level stuff but project pages return permission denied. Token in header looks fine according to their devs.
anya: can you paste the exact repro steps and the auth headers they send (redact keys)?
sam: customer steps: 1) login via SSO (Okta) 2) click project dropdown -> select 'acme-prod' 3) get 403 UI card. They sent this curl snippet: ```curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer ey.REDACTED\" -H \"X-Client: acme-web\" https://console.redwood.ai/api/projects/acme-prod```
kevin: thx. any recent idp claim mapping changes for that org? claims -> project_access or teams?
sam: support ticket says they recently renamed an Okta group from "acme-prod-admins" to "acme-prod-admins-v2" last night. SCIM sync looks green.
julia: sounds like a claim->role mapping drift + our claim cache holding old mapping. I bet gatekeeper evaluated the cached claims and didn't pick up the new group name. can you repro with their token and check /auth/debug endpoint?
sam: tried debug: token introspect shows groups: ["acme-prod-admins-v2"], scope: ["console:read","console:write:projects"] but gatekeeper log for the request shows matched_groups: ["acme-prod-admins"] (old).
anya: aha — claim cache TTL might be long and not invalidated on SCIM rename. what's the gatekeeper cache TTL for claims for that region?
kevin: default is 10m but we have per-org override for enterprise orgs settable; for ACME it's 1h due to past flapping, looks like we accidentally set sticky cache when running the mass-rename.
julia: immediate workaround: invalidate claim cache for that org (admin API) or have the user do a full logout -> re-login which will refresh session claims. can ops run: ```POST /admin/orgs/acme/invalidate-claim-cache```
sam: ops ran the invalidate endpoint and user still hit 403 immediately after — logs show gatekeeper still matched old group for that request id 0a1b2c3d.
kevin: probable race: old worker node still has sticky in-memory cache and didn't receive the invalidation broadcast. need to roll the gatekeeper group cache or send a pubsub invalidation.
anya: @support-bot can you create an escalation ticket and tag eng-infra + eng-runtime? include request id 0a1b2c3d, sample auth headers (redacted), and the gatekeeper logs snippets.
support-bot: created ticket SUP-12345 and paged #eng-infra and #eng-runtime. ETA 2h. :rotating_light:
sam: customer updated that full logout -> browser hard refresh -> login allowed access. they accepted workaround but want permanent fix.
julia: plan: 1) investigate why invalidation didn't propagate (pubsub dead-letter?) 2) add a short-term hotfix to broadcast invalidation to all regions, 3) follow-up: make claim-cache honor SCIM rename hooks so we auto-invalidate mapping on group rename.
kevin: I'll pick up the hotfix (rolling restart of gatekeeper cache process + ensure invalidation hook) and post progress in the ticket.
anya: leaving a note for support: workaround = ask user to log out and re-login, or we can run admin invalidate for org and do a quick rolling restart if needed. mark thread as escalated. :white_check_mark:
